**Visual analysis:**

- **Affected plant part**: Wheat spike (head/ear)
- **Key features**:
  - Orange/salmon-pink coloration on the glumes (outer coverings of the spikelets)
  - White cottony mycelium/fungal growth visible mixed in with the orange tissue
  - Upper portion of the spike is bleached/dead (tan-white)
  - Lower spikelets remain green (partial infection)
  - Some dark/black areas at the base of infected spikelets

**Reasoning:**

The combination of salmon-pink to orange discoloration of the glumes, visible cottony fungal mycelium on the spike, and partial bleaching (whitened spikelets above the infection point while lower spikelets remain green) is the classic presentation of **Fusarium Head Blight / Head Scab**. This disease, caused by *Fusarium graminearum*, characteristically produces:
- Pink/salmon/orange mycelium and sporodochia on infected glumes
- Premature bleaching of affected spikelets
- Partial head infection ("tombstone" kernels above the point of entry)

Other possibilities were ruled out:
- **Stem Rust / Wheat Stem Rust**: Would show discrete orange-brown uredinia pustules on stems/leaves, not this pattern
- **Loose Smut**: Would replace the entire grain mass with dark powdery smut spores
- **Dwarf Bunt**: Would produce globose bunt balls replacing kernels
- **Black Chaff**: Would show dark black streaking on chaff, different from the orange mycelium seen here
